cold_open.hook: OpenAI's losing senior execs right before going public—the company's basically doing a pre-IPO refresh that looks less like strategy and more like musical chairs.

markets.macro_note: Broad rally on softer inflation expectations; mega-cap tech mixed, but streaming and software outperforming.

big_story.story_title: OpenAI sheds senior execs in pre-IPO refresh
big_story.angle: OpenAI is hemorrhaging senior talent weeks before a potential IPO—not a sign of confidence. What does it say about the company's actual governance and whether Altman has real control, or if the board is finally pushing back?

quick_hits.angle: Investors suing Selena Gomez's mental health startup for fraud—the irony of a mental health company allegedly lying to its backers is almost too on-the-nose.
Data breaches already past last year's total with AI accelerating the problem—companies are building faster than they can secure, and AI is the new vector.
China's backflip robots are impressive engineering theater—cool to watch, impossible to monetize, and that's the entire Chinese robotics story right now.
Tesla bought out its Swedish strikers instead of negotiating—Musk's labor strategy is 'if you won't work for me, I'll just buy you off,' which works until it doesn't.

odd_thing.joke_angle: A Cold War movie that gives Reagan too much credit—basically the opposite problem every other Reagan movie has, which means someone finally made the contrarian take that nobody asked for.

yesterday_callback.topic: Musk and Zuckerberg both launching new AI models simultaneously—less about technical breakthrough, more about who gets the narrative
yesterday_callback.fresh_take: OpenAI's exec exodus suggests the AI model wars aren't just about who ships first—they're about who can actually keep a team together long enough to ship anything.
